About
## About me
Geoinformatics engineer, based in Dehradun.
### My story
I've been doing geospatial research for more than four years, including work at DRDO and at Survey of India's Geodetic & Research Branch. Most of that work is about taking raw spatial data and automating the steps between the data and a decision.
At Survey of India I manage two wings. The NSRF Wing processes GNSS CORS data from 1023+ reference stations, and the HPL Wing maintains India's national vertical datum. My scripts brought GNSS processing down from 7 days to 3 days per station, and my levelling adjustment software made HPL computation about 100 times faster. QA/QC checks such as the Tau test and global statistical validation run inside the scripts, so manual errors don't get through.
At DRDO's Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment I processed about 3 million LiDAR points and 32 hyperspectral bands. I used them to build flood inundation models and terrain vulnerability assessments for defence planning and disaster preparedness.
I also started the Geospatial Technology Club at NSUT. It grew to 200+ members from across India, and we brought in industry professionals for talks and workshops.
I try to write code that someone else can pick up later: clean, documented, and built to keep working as the data grows. The work I enjoy most is research where the numbers have to be right.
Looking for
I'm looking for research roles, consulting work, and startups working on hard geospatial problems with real users. If that sounds like your team, get in touch.
Get in touch

### Approach
Three things that shape how I work.
#### Location technology
Everything I do starts with GIS, GNSS and remote sensing. That means GAMIT/GLOBK and PRIDE PPP-AR processing for 1023+ CORS stations, LiDAR and hyperspectral analysis, and drone mapping.
#### From data to decisions
My pipelines have QA/QC checks built in (Tau test, global statistical validation), and they cut GNSS processing from 7 days to 3 days per station and made levelling (HPL) computation about 100x faster with a real-time adjustment software for 1,00,000+ observations.
#### Work that gets used
I did flood risk planning for defence at DRDO, and I'm building SolarSight and Baadh Mitra at Uday GeoAnalytics Consultancy for rooftop solar and village flood alerts. I also started a Geospatial Technology Club at NSUT that grew to 200+ members.

GIS Engineer, Survey of India

04 / ProjectSurvey of India, NSRF Wing (G&RB)
## GNSS CORS network data processing
Survey of India, NSRF Wing (G&RB)
Photo: LubGua987, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
- Python
- GAMIT/GLOBK
- PRIDE PPP-AR
- GNSS
- RINEX
- Automation
Reference stations
1023+
Saved weekly
12 h
Accuracy
cm
### Overview
I wrote Python pipelines that download and preprocess GNSS data automatically, which saves 12 hours of manual work every week. The multi-day datasets are then processed in GAMIT/GLOBK and PRIDE PPP-AR to centimeter-level accuracy across 1023+ reference stations.
The NSRF Wing at Survey of India handles GNSS CORS data for 1023+ reference stations. With the automation in place, processing takes 3 days per station instead of 7, and 365-day datasets run in batches.
Station coordinates are derived in both static and kinematic modes. Before processing, every observation file is checked for cycle slips, data completeness and satellite geometry. I also worked with a team of 5 geodetic engineers to standardise data collection across all 1023+ stations, and I document the processing methods so the wider team can run them.
### Tech stack
- Python
- GAMIT/GLOBK
- PRIDE PPP-AR
- RINEX
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
GNSS data from 1023+ CORS reference stations was being processed by hand.
02 Data
Multi-day GNSS datasets (RINEX), including 365-day datasets, from CORS reference stations.
03 Method
GAMIT/GLOBK and PRIDE PPP-AR processing in static and kinematic modes for centimeter-level accuracy. Quality control covers cycle slip detection, data completeness checks and satellite geometry assessment.
04 System
Python pipelines for automated GNSS data acquisition, preprocessing and batch processing.
05 Result
3 days per station instead of 7, and 12 hours of manual work saved each week.
### Results
- Centimeter-level accuracy across 1023+ reference stations.
- Processing time reduced from 7 days to 3 days per station.
- 12 hours of manual processing saved every week.
- One set of data collection protocols across 1023+ stations, agreed with a team of 5 geodetic engineers.

04 / ProjectSurvey of India, HPL Wing (G&RB)
## High Precision Levelling (HPL) network processing
Survey of India, HPL Wing (G&RB)
Photo: Cvstr, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
- HPL
- Levelling
- Geodesy
- Height Datum
- Loop Closure
- QC/QA
GCPs processed
1,00,780
Faster computation
~100x
Vertical datum
National
### Overview
I processed and validated High Precision Levelling data for 1,00,780 Ground Control Points (GCPs) across India, for the Geodesy & Research Branch (G&RB) of Survey of India. The work covers height datum computation, loop closure analysis and correcting systematic errors across the levelling network, so the national vertical datum stays accurate.
I also automated the geopotential number, standard deviation and Helmert orthometric height calculations, with QA/QC (Tau test, global statistical validation) built in. An adjustment software processes all 1,00,000+ observations together in real time, making HPL computation about 100x faster.
### Tech stack
- High Precision Levelling
- Helmert orthometric heights
- Geopotential numbers
- Tau test
- Python
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
Maintain the accuracy of India's national vertical datum.
02 Data
High Precision Levelling data for 1,00,780 Ground Control Points across India.
03 Method
Height datum computation, loop closure analysis and systematic error correction; geopotential number, standard deviation and Helmert orthometric height computation.
04 System
Automated calculations with QA/QC built in (Tau test and global statistical validation).
05 Result
HPL computation is about 100x faster.
### Results
- 1,00,780 Ground Control Points processed and validated.
- 1,00,000+ observations adjusted together in real time, about 100x faster.
- Fewer manual errors, thanks to built-in QA/QC checks.

## SolarSight
Rooftop Solar Potential Assessment Platform
Photo: Kolforn, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
- GIS
- Web
- Solar
- Maps
Assessment time
< 2 min
PDF report
7 pages
Cost to users
Free
### Overview
SolarSight is a web platform that works out how much rooftop solar makes sense for a home anywhere in India. You give your location and answer a few questions about your roof. An AI engine then combines real-time NASA satellite data on solar radiation with your region's electricity tariff, and sizes a system for you with a cost breakdown and payback period.
It covers all 36 states and union territories and sorts every location into one of five solar climate zones. Panel suggestions come from 50+ MNRE-approved models by 18 manufacturers, and the PM Surya Ghar subsidy is calculated automatically for your state. It's always free for homeowners: the money comes from solar installers, not from selling user data. In under 2 minutes you get panel count, savings, subsidy, payback and installer leads, in a 7-page PDF report you can share on WhatsApp.
Visit solarsight.in
### Tech stack
- NASA solar radiation data
- Regional electricity tariffs
- MNRE-approved panel database
- PM Surya Ghar subsidy calculator
- AI-powered analysis
- PDF report generation
- Email and WhatsApp delivery
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
Give any homeowner in India a full rooftop solar assessment, free.
02 Data
Real-time NASA satellite data on solar radiation, regional electricity tariffs, state subsidy rules, and a database of 50+ MNRE-approved panels from 18 manufacturers.
03 Method
An AI engine combines the solar radiation data, the tariff and the user's answers about their roof, places the location in one of five solar climate zones, and sizes the system.
04 System
Three steps: enter your location, answer a few questions about your roof, and get the full report by email or WhatsApp, with panel count, savings, subsidy, payback, installer leads and panel suggestions.
05 Result
A full assessment in under 2 minutes and a 7-page PDF report, free.
### Results
- Full rooftop solar assessment in under 2 minutes.
- Panel count, savings, subsidy, payback and installer leads for every address.
- Available in all 36 states and union territories.
- Delivered as a 7-page PDF report, shareable via WhatsApp.
- Free to use.
From a real report · Bisauli, Uttar Pradesh · 25 August 2026
View the full 7-page report (PDF)

## Baadh Mitra
Flood early warnings for villages
Photo: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, GODL-India, via Wikimedia Commons
- Web
- Flood
- WhatsApp
- Data
Pilot villages
States
Alert channel
WhatsApp
### Overview
Baadh Mitra sends flood warnings to villages through WhatsApp, so people get them without installing an app. It combines real-time weather data with flood forecasts, and uses AI to write alerts in local languages that arrive in time to act on.
The system is still in development, with completion expected around 2028. The plan is a pilot in 50 villages across Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Assam, followed by a phased nationwide rollout.
### Tech stack
- WhatsApp
- Real-time weather data
- Flood forecasting data
- AI-powered alerts
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
Villages need flood warnings early enough to act on them.
02 Data
Real-time weather data and flood forecasting information.
03 Method
AI generates a personalised alert.
04 System
Alerts go straight to village WhatsApp groups in regional languages. There's no app to install.
05 Result
Pilot launch in 50 villages across Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Assam, followed by a phased nationwide rollout.
### Results
- Pilot: 50 villages across Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Assam.
- Alerts in regional languages that arrive in time to act on.
- No app to install.

04 / ProjectUday GeoAnalytics ConsultancyIn Development
## UGD LULC Engine
Land use classification for all of India
Photo: Sentinel Hub (contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data), CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
- GIS
- Deep Learning
- Python
- Data
Validation accuracy
98.1%
Architecture phases
Sub-products
### Overview
A deep learning pipeline, now over 1 lakh lines of code, that classifies land use and land cover across India. It's trained on EuroSAT and reaches 98.1% validation accuracy. The pipeline runs in 6 phases, and labelling is done inside QGIS.
Four products are planned on top of it: GreenWatch (encroachment alerts), VillageLens (land use stats for each revenue village), CarbonSight (carbon credit estimates) and ReportGen (automatic bilingual MoEFCC/EIA reports).
### Tech stack
- Deep Learning (PyTorch)
- EuroSAT
- QGIS
- LULC classification
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
Land Use Land Cover classification at pan-India scale.
02 Data
EuroSAT, with a QGIS-integrated labeling workflow.
03 Method
A deep learning pipeline in 6 phases, with full validation.
04 System
Four products built on the engine: GreenWatch (encroachment alerts), VillageLens (land use stats for each revenue village), CarbonSight (carbon credit estimates) and ReportGen (automatic bilingual MoEFCC/EIA reports).
05 Result
98.1% validation accuracy on EuroSAT.
### Results
- 98.1% validation accuracy.
- Four sub-products planned on one engine.
All projects Discuss a project

Any site
### Overview
Kuaan Mitra estimates how likely a borewell is to succeed at any location. It's meant for farmers and groundwater planners, and it runs on free government geological, hydrogeological and remote sensing data. The aim is fewer expensive failed drillings.
### Tech stack
- Government geological data
- Hydrogeological data
- Remote sensing data
- AI prediction model
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
Costly drilling failures and water investment risks for farmers and groundwater planners.
02 Data
Free government geological, hydrogeological and remote sensing data.
03 Method
An AI model predicts the chance of success.
04 System
A borewell site-suitability predictor that returns success probability at any location.
05 Result
Fewer costly drilling failures. In development, with completion expected around 2028.
### Results
- Success probability for any location.
- Fewer costly drilling failures.

## Jameen Mitra
Land records, explained on WhatsApp
Photo: Bhullargraphic, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
- Web
- WhatsApp
- Land Records
- Data
Phase 1 states
Channel
WhatsApp
Summaries
Plain text
### Overview
Jameen Mitra is a WhatsApp chatbot for India's Bhulekh land records. You send your plot number and get back a short, plain-language summary of who owns the land, so you don't need to know legal terms to read it. Phase 1 covers UP, Bihar and Rajasthan.
### Tech stack
- WhatsApp chatbot
- Bhulekh land records
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
Rural citizens need land ownership information from India's Bhulekh land record system without needing legal literacy.
02 Data
India's Bhulekh land records.
03 Method
Ownership records are summarised in plain language.
04 System
A WhatsApp chatbot: send a plot number, receive the summary.
05 Result
Phase 1 covers UP, Bihar and Rajasthan. In development, with completion expected around 2028.
### Results
- Plain-language summaries of land ownership.
- Phase 1: UP, Bihar and Rajasthan.

04 / ProjectDRDO, Ministry of Defence
## Flood risk mapping and spatial analysis
DRDO, Ministry of Defence
Photo: MODIS Land Rapid Response Team, NASA GSFC, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
- QGIS
- Flood Risk
- DEM
- Spatial Analysis
- Thematic Mapping
GIS layers
5+
Sea-level-rise scenario
1 m
Analysis platform
QGIS
### Overview
I mapped flood risk in QGIS from terrain and elevation layers, to find the areas that flood above a 1 m sea level rise. Combining 5+ layers, including terrain, elevation and drainage, showed where the most vulnerable zones were.
I did this as a research intern at the Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment (DGRE), DRDO, Chandigarh, from July to December 2024. The inundation models showed how vulnerable the terrain was, and fed into defence planning and disaster preparedness.
### Tech stack
- QGIS
- DEM
- Terrain and drainage layers
- Thematic mapping
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
Find the areas that flood above a 1 m sea level rise.
02 Data
5+ geospatial layers including terrain, elevation and drainage.
03 Method
Multi-layer spatial analysis of terrain and elevation-based layers.
04 System
Several thematic flood risk maps and spatial visualisations in QGIS, plus flood inundation models, prepared for regional flood assessment.
05 Result
A map of vulnerable zones, used for defence planning and disaster preparedness.
### Results
- Flood-prone areas identified above a 1 m sea level rise.
- Vulnerable zones mapped from 5+ geospatial layers.
- A set of thematic flood risk maps for regional flood assessment.

## LiDAR and hyperspectral data analysis
DRDO, Ministry of Defence
Photo: FuzzyGeo, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
- Python
- LiDAR
- Spectral Python
- laspy
- Point Cloud
- Hyperspectral
LiDAR points
~3M
Hyperspectral bands
Processing
Python
### Overview
I analysed a dense LiDAR point cloud of about 3 million points with Spectral Python to study the terrain, and wrote Python scripts to preprocess and filter the large LiDAR and hyperspectral datasets.
The data came in .pix and .hdr formats: about 3 million LiDAR points and 32 hyperspectral bands, handled in Python with Spectral Python and laspy. This was at the Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment (DGRE), DRDO.
### Tech stack
- Python
- Spectral Python
- laspy
- .pix / .hdr formats
### Process
Problem → Data → Method → System → Result
01 Problem
Study terrain characteristics from high-density LiDAR and hyperspectral data.
02 Data
~3 million LiDAR points and 32 hyperspectral bands (.pix, .hdr formats).
03 Method
Analysis with Spectral Python and laspy.
04 System
Python scripts for preprocessing and filtering large LiDAR and hyperspectral datasets.
05 Result
Analytical outputs and visualisations that helped interpret the terrain and supported environmental analysis for defence research.
### Results
- ~3 million LiDAR points analyzed.
- 32 hyperspectral bands processed.
- Faster data handling, thanks to the preprocessing and filtering scripts.
